latin: Infinitas dei per superexcedentiam ad esse intellectuale et uiam mysticae theologiae probari potest, et ad id probandum omnis alia uia inefficax est.
latin_note: 1486 prints 'super excedentiam' as two words; the Emendationes errorum corrects it to 'per superexcedentiam', which 1487 adopts. Text follows the emended reading.
translation: God's infinity can only be established by his surpassing excess over intellectual being and by the path of mystical theology; every other route to proving it fails.
translation_note: 'mysticae theologiae' points to Pseudo-Dionysius's negative way; sense checked.
